title: Field-replacement trigger matrix and competitive signal assimilation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: define a repeatable, partially-automated playbook that converts competitive-model signals and field telemetry into deterministic 'replacement triggers' that can initiate staged fallbacks, procurement alerts, or Canopy-managed rollbacks.

Background: customers and platform teams increasingly need guarantees that service-level behavior won't silently degrade when a model provider changes availability, pricing, or behavior. Existing work covers model scouting and fallback lists, but we lack a compact decision surface and operational thresholds for automated guardrails. This ticket scopes the product-ready trigger matrix and the signal assimilation pipeline used by Console and the Operations runbook.

Scope:
- Enumerate signal sources: provider status pages, cloud quota alerts, pricing spikes (billing feed), model-quality regressions (prompt-suite delta), latency/CPU/GPU tail metrics, embedding drift (downstream retrieval precision), third-party supply signals (release notes, repo tags).
- Define normalized signal schema and weighting (time-decay, severity, coverage) so we can score a model's 'operational health' as a single percentile.
- Propose discrete trigger thresholds and mapped actions (soft alert -> canary routing -> automatic fallback -> procurement escalation).
- Create Console wireframes for an actionable alert card showing signal composition and recommended steps.
- Integrate with Linear alerting (auto-create PM/SEV tickets) and procurement playbooks for Dedicated/Private sales teams.

Non-goals: fully automated vendor swaps without human sign-off for high-impact enterprise customers; building new model inference connectors (we will reuse existing adapter layer).

Design trade-offs and assumptions:
- Conservative defaults: automated fallbacks limited to non-sensitive customers; enterprise customers default to manual approval unless configured.
- Weighting: quality regressions (semantic drift) should outweigh transient infra noise; we apply a 15-minute smoothing window for latency and a 24-hour rolling window for quality deltas.
- Cost vs availability: low-cost fallback models acceptable for read-only features; for safety-critical paths require parity checks before swap.

Success metrics:
- Time from detected signal to completed trigger action (target ≤ 15 minutes for automated non-enterprise fallbacks).
- Reduction in customer-impacting incidents due to model outages by 30% in Q2 after rollout.
- False-positive trigger rate < 5% after first 6 weeks of tuning.

Deliverables:
- Trigger matrix CSV + normalization rules.
- Console alert card mock + copy.
- Signal ingestion spec (format + retention).
- Linear automation recipe and sample Slack/escalation message templates.

Operational notes:
- Will pair with Research to define quality-signal prompt sets and continuous eval thresholds.
- Security will review alert data retention and PII exposure (signal payloads may contain sanitized prompt IDs and sample outputs).
acceptance_criteria: Complete enumerated list of signal sources and one-paragraph rationale for each
Normalized scoring algorithm documented and reproducible (CSV example + calculation steps)
Trigger matrix (threshold -> action mapping) exported as CSV and integrated into a Console mock endpoint
Linear automation recipe that can create an incident ticket with pre-filled fields and recommended runbook steps
Sign-off from Research on the semantic-drift thresholds and from Security on retention/censoring rules
